div.head: II Eg 5
div.ab: ⁊ healde man ælces Sunnandæges freols fram nóntide þæs Sæternesdæges oð ðæs Monandæges lihtinge, be þam wite, þe domboc tæcð, ⁊ ælcne oðerne mæssedæg swa he bebodan beo.
⁊ healde mon ælces Sunnandæges freolsunga fram [Sæternesdæges] nontide oð Monandæges lihtinge, be þam wíte, ðe seo dómboc tæcð, ⁊ ælcne oðerne mæssedæg, swa he beboden beo.

Et sollenne diei dominice conseruetur ab hora nona Sabbati usque ad lucidum diei Lune, super forisfacturam, quam liber iudiciorum dicit (docet), et omnis alia festiuitas, sicut a sacerdote nunciabitur.

[Be freolsdægum ⁊ fæstenum.] [Ld] ⁊ healde man ælces Sunnandæges freolsunga fram Sæternesdæges nontide oð Monandæges lihtinge, be þam wite ðe seo domboc tæce, ⁊ ælcne oðerne mæssedæg swa he beboden sy.
And healde man ælces Sunnandæges freols fram nontide þæs Sæternesdæges oð ðæs Monandæges lihtinge, be þam wite, þe domboc tæcð, and ælcne oðerne mæssedæg, swa he bebodan beo.

And every Sunday shall be observed as a festival from noonday on Saturday till dawn on Monday, under pain of the penalty which the written law prescribes; and every other feast-day according to the regulations appointed for it.

And each Sunday holy day is to be observed as the written law instructs from midafternoon on Saturday until dawn on Monday, lest a penalty be incurred, and every other feast day just as is ordained for it.
And every Sunday shall be observed as a festival from Saturday noon until dawn on Monday, under pain of the punishment which the law-book prescribes; and every other festival as it is enjoined.

(Von Feiertagen und Fasten. Ld) Und man halte die Feier jedes Sonntages von Mittagszeit des Sonnabends bis zum Morgengrauen des Montags, bei der Strafe, welche das Gesetzbuch vorschreibt, und jedes andere Kirchenfest, wie es geboten ist.

(Of feast-days and fasts. Ld) And let the festival of every Sunday be kept from noon on Saturday until dawn on Monday, on pain of the fine which the law-book prescribes, and every other feast-day as it is commanded.
div.note: In A, ‘Sæternesdæges’ was added above the line by a later hand. Liebermann compares Ine 3.
